digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter (Jira integration) — 429 sweep, config validation, and parity with DC
propositions: Cloud transport has four distinct 429 behaviours across two levels (direct REST, ACLI subprocess, dispatch-wrapped, non-retrying apply phases) that require per-layer enumeration and assertion rather than a uniform property, because some are deliberately retried and others are not.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be explicitly enumerated and classified by transport seam (subprocess, pooled REST, bare urlopen) and dispatch level, with duplicate-write safety documented for known deliberate retries, as an enumeration prevents ellipsis-based inheritance of retry logic.
Cloud does not reject non-HTTPS base URLs or fail loudly on missing credentials, in contrast to DC; these must be absence-documented as tests or handled as bugs if they are actual gaps.

Cloud's probe hardcodes resolved-status names while DC reads them from configuration; the decision whether Cloud needs a runtime hook or can rely on workflow constraints must be documented at the definition site, not only in the tracker.
DC exposes no user-search method aliases and degrades safely to string matching; Cloud must assert this degradation path is tested and does not raise on the DC-shaped side.
